title: Respecting reduced motion
summary: prefers-reduced-motion swaps a sliding banner for a simple fade for people who ask for less motion.
explanation: Some people get dizzy or distracted by movement on screen and turn on a 'reduce motion' setting in their operating system. CSS can read it with @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

Here the banner normally slides in from the side. Under reduced motion it uses a different keyframes rule that only fades, so the information still appears gently but nothing travels across the screen.
Turning motion off is not always the goal: keep feedback that helps (a fade, a colour change) and drop movement that is only decoration.
tryThis: Turn on 'reduce motion' in your system settings (Windows: Settings › Accessibility › Visual effects › Animation effects off) and re-apply the example.
Change the slide distance from -40px to -200px.
Inside the media query, set animation: none: the banner simply appears.
